headline: DISCOVERY MINING BUYS MCEWEN'S LAST TIMMINS HOLDINGS — $55M DEAL DEEPENS DISTRICT CONSOLIDATION
source_name: Junior Mining Network / Discovery Mining (TSX: DSV, OTCQX: DSVSF)
snippet: Discovery Mining Ltd. (TSX: DSV) entered into an asset purchase agreement on October 10-11, 2026 to acquire certain Timmins mineral properties from McEwen Inc., with consideration of $5 million in cash and $50 million payable in common shares of Discovery — a $55 million total package. The deal extends Discovery's aggressive Timmins district consolidation thesis, which began in January 2025 with the $425 million acquisition of Newmont's Porcupine Complex and continued in mid-2026 with Glencore's Kidd Operations. McEwen Inc.'s Timmins land package has historically included the Buffalo Ankerite, Fuller, Davidson Tisdale, and Paymaster properties — geological addresses that sit adjacent to the Dome and Hollinger-McIntyre systems Discovery already controls. For retail investors tracking the TSX-V and TSX mining sector, Discovery is executing a historically rare play: consolidating multiple formerly major Timmins gold operations under one management team at a time when gold near $4,200/oz makes sub-economic historical deposits economically viable again. The share-heavy consideration structure is notable — it implies Discovery's management is confident in its own stock and isn't diluting with cheap paper, which is a positive capital discipline signal. Closing is expected in October 2026, subject to TSX and regulatory approvals.

headline: AURA MINERALS SMASHES Q3 PRODUCTION RECORD — 95,557 GEO MARKS BEST NINE-MONTH RUN IN COMPANY HISTORY
source_name: Junior Mining Network / Aura Minerals (NASDAQ: AUGO, TSX: ORA)
snippet: Aura Minerals (NASDAQ: AUGO) reported preliminary Q3 2026 production of 95,557 gold equivalent ounces (GEO) across its six operating mines — a record quarterly output, up 27% from Q2 2026 and 29% from Q3 2025. Sales reached 93,742 GEO in the quarter. Nine-month 2026 production of 253,131 GEO is the highest in the company's history at any comparable period. The standout performer was its MSG mine, where production rose 85% quarter-on-quarter as a recovery program advanced. Borborema in Brazil, which had posted lower Q2 grades due to planned mine sequencing, appears to have normalized in Q3. At gold prices near $4,200 per ounce, the Q3 record translates to approximately $400 million in quarterly gold equivalent revenue before costs — the most robust revenue quarter in Aura's history. For retail investors benchmarking junior-to-mid-tier producers, Aura's Q3 print sets an early, high bar for the October-November earnings season. The company reports formal Q3 financial results later in Q4 2026; full-year guidance has not been revised but appears comfortably achievable.

headline: SILVER DEFICIT WIDENS FOR 6TH STRAIGHT YEAR — 46.3 MOZ SHORTFALL DRAINS 762 MOZ FROM GLOBAL STOCKPILES
snippet: A GlobeNewswire release dated October 9, 2026 — citing the World Silver Survey 2026 published by the Silver Institute with Metals Focus — forecasts a 46.3 million ounce silver supply deficit for 2026, up from 40.3 million ounces in 2025, marking the sixth consecutive year of global above-ground stock drawdowns. The cumulative drawdown since 2021 now stands at 762.1 million ounces, a figure that is historically unprecedented in the silver market. Total demand for 2026 is forecast at 1.11 billion ounces even as total demand falls 2% from 2025, as solar panel manufacturing, EV charging infrastructure, and AI data center electrical requirements absorb incremental supply. The six-year streak is particularly important context for the current silver price correction from its January record near $121/oz to current levels around $60: the structural supply deficit remains intact regardless of paper market short-term price action. For junior silver miners and companies with significant silver byproduct credits on TSX-V and ASX, this data supports the bull case for sustained silver prices well above the $50 floor — the physical market is not in surplus, even if Western ETF flows and macro pressure suggest otherwise.

headline: CALEDONIA MINING CUTS BLANKET GUIDANCE AGAIN — AISC RISES TO $2,850/OZ AS ZIMBABWE MINE HITS Q3 WALL
snippet: Caledonia Mining (NYSE: CMCL) issued a Q3 2026 production update on approximately October 10 cutting Blanket Mine gold production guidance to 69,000-72,500 ounces for 2026 — down from the prior 72,000-76,500 ounce range — while raising all-in sustaining cost (AISC) guidance to $2,650-$2,850 per ounce sold from the prior $2,500-$2,700 range. On-mine cost per ounce was raised to $1,700-$1,900. Capital expenditure guidance was reduced to $94.3 million from $103.3 million, as a 132kV power line delivery slips to 2027. The company described Blanket as 'robust and cash-generative' and said Q4 operational steps including a seven-day shift and potential oxide mining at K-pits support a stronger 2027 outlook. At gold near $4,200/oz, Blanket remains cash-flow positive even at $2,850/oz AISC — the margin is approximately $1,350/oz. But the guidance cut is the third revision in 2026 and continues a pattern of softening operational performance that began with a January AISC estimate of $2,100-$2,300. Retail investors holding small-cap African gold producers should note that Caledonia's original 2026 guidance implied cost discipline that the realized trajectory has not delivered.

headline: ROCK TECH LITHIUM ONTARIO PLANT: FEASIBILITY PUTS CAPEX AT C$596M FOR 30,000 T/Y — STUDY CALLS IT 'HIGHLY COMPETITIVE'
source_name: Mining Weekly / Rock Tech Lithium (TSX: RCK)
snippet: Rock Tech Lithium (TSX: RCK) released preliminary feasibility results on October 8, 2026 for its Red Rock lithium hydroxide converter plant in Ontario, with total capital cost estimated at C$596 million — comprising C$546 million direct costs and C$50 million owner's costs, with a ±20% tolerance. The study, being completed by China CEC Engineering, targets 30,000 tonnes per year of lithium salts, with the final feasibility results due by year-end 2026. The 'highly competitive' characterization in the release headline reflects the significant step-down from Rock Tech's earlier C$680 million estimate following design optimizations, and potentially from a still-older US$1 billion figure. A C$200 million anchor investment from BMI Group covers roughly one-third of the capex, with additional financing — likely including a government component given the plant's critical minerals mandate — needed to reach financial close. Construction is targeted to begin in H2 2027, with Red Rock positioned to supply battery-grade lithium hydroxide into North American EV supply chains ahead of the IRA's critical minerals sourcing requirements. For investors tracking Canadian lithium infrastructure, Red Rock is one of very few fully-permitted, near-shovel-ready conversion facilities in North America.

headline: SIGMA LITHIUM BACK ONLINE IN BRAZIL — APPEALS COURT UPHOLDS GROTA DO CIRILO ENVIRONMENTAL LICENCES
source_name: Mining Weekly / Sigma Lithium (NASDAQ: SGML, TSX: SGML)
snippet: Sigma Lithium (NASDAQ: SGML) announced on October 7, 2026 that a Brazilian federal appeals court has overturned a September emergency order that had suspended its environmental licences at the Grota do Cirilo project in Minas Gerais, allowing the company to resume mining and processing operations immediately. The suspension had been sought by the Federation of Quilombola Communities of Minas Gerais, which argued the mine affects the nearby Bau Quilombola community. Sigma disputed the order as procedurally improper, and the appeals court agreed. A separate labour dispute over waste pile shutdowns initiated by Brazilian inspectors in December 2025 remains unresolved but is on a different legal track. Sigma's 2027 production target of 330,000 tonnes of lithium oxide concentrate annualized does not require additional mining capacity, suggesting the September suspension did not materially alter its production economics. The resumption removes an acute supply-disruption risk that had depressed the stock — retail investors should note that Brazilian permitting litigation is an ongoing operational risk for any Latin American lithium developer, not a one-time event.

headline: MAGNA MINING APPROVES LEVACK RESTART — 7.3-YEAR PEA GIVES SUDBURY NICKEL MINE A VIABLE PATH BACK
source_name: Junior Mining Network / Magna Mining (TSX: NICU)
snippet: Magna Mining (TSX: NICU) released a Preliminary Economic Assessment for its Levack Mine in the Sudbury Basin on approximately October 8, 2026, and immediately announced the board's approval to proceed with a production restart. The PEA envisions a 7.3-year commercial production life at a 2,141 tonne-per-day mining rate, accessed via a new surface ramp to shallower deposits and the refurbished No. 2 shaft for hoisting high-grade footwall material. The resource base underpinning the PEA includes 6.1 million tonnes of Indicated at 3.5% copper equivalent and 5.2 million tonnes of Inferred at 3.6% copper equivalent, as established in a November 2025 resource estimate. The PEA excludes the R2 Footwall Zone, which remains open and represents additional upside. Levack's copper-nickel-precious metals profile aligns with critical minerals mandates in both Canada and the US, where primary nickel and copper production from Tier 1 jurisdictions commands an offtake premium. The board's approval to proceed ahead of a Prefeasibility Study is an aggressive capital deployment decision that signals management confidence in Levack's economics at current metal prices and the plant availability nearby in Sudbury.

headline: FORTUNA Q3 2026: 69,665 GEO FALLS BELOW Q2 PACE — SÉGUÉLA 30% EXPANSION NOD TARGETS 200,000 OZ BY 2028
source_name: GlobeNewswire / Fortuna Mining (NYSE: FSM, TSX: FVI)
snippet: Fortuna Mining (NYSE: FSM, TSX: FVI) reported Q3 2026 gold equivalent production of 69,665 ounces on October 7 — down 3.5% from Q2's 72,217 GEO and 3.9% below Q3 2025's 72,462 GEO, while nine-month production of 214,754 GEO keeps the company on track for its 2026 annual guidance of 281,000-305,000 GEO. The Séguéla mine in Côte d'Ivoire produced 33,744 oz in Q3, below Q2's 41,683 oz, due to mine sequencing through lower-grade transitional ore. Lindero in Argentina was the bright spot, with output rising 25% quarter-on-quarter to 26,024 oz. The most significant strategic development in the release is board approval for a 30% expansion of the Séguéla processing plant, targeting annual gold production of over 200,000 ounces from H2 2028 — which would make Séguéla alone larger than Fortuna's current total company output. For investors evaluating mid-tier producers with organic growth pipelines, the Séguéla expansion at $4,200 gold is compelling on paper, though the timeline to H2 2028 means two years of construction and commissioning execution risk. Fortuna's total safety record (TRIFR 1.20) improved fractionally quarter-on-quarter.

headline: RARE EARTH STOCKS ROUT ENTERS SECOND SESSION — USAR AND MP MATERIALS DOWN 5%, SECTOR OFFERS NO SPECIFIC CATALYST
snippet: Rare earth mining and processing stocks suffered a sector-wide selloff across October 7-8, 2026, with USA Rare Earth (NASDAQ: USAR) and MP Materials (NYSE: MP) each losing approximately 5% over two sessions, Critical Metals dropping 3%, and the VanEck Rare Earth and Strategic Metals ETF falling 3%. Analyst commentary attributed the moves to fading near-term catalysts and broader risk-off positioning in critical minerals equities rather than any company-specific news — with the divergence between builders (pre-revenue) and producers (MP Materials) tighter than usual, suggesting macro-driven selling rather than a differentiated assessment. The selloff coincides with USAR's transition to a new CEO: Thras Moraitis (former Serra Verde CEO) assumed leadership October 1 following the company's $2.8 billion Serra Verde acquisition, with Phase 1a commercial magnet production at Stillwater targeting 600 metric tons per year by end 2026. The $1.6 billion in Commerce Department backing announced for USAR's mine-to-magnet buildout has not arrested the share price slide, illustrating the gap between policy support and market sentiment in the critical minerals space. China's export control suspension (extended through January 10, 2027) is providing temporary supply relief while simultaneously postponing the catalyst that would most directly validate the Western rare earth investment thesis.

headline: SILVER BULLET MINES HITS 41.1 G/T AU IN ARIZONA — FIRST ASSAYS FROM COLUMBIA/GOLD QUEEN COMPLEX DELIVERED
source_name: Mining Stock Education / Silver Bullet Mines Corp. (TSXV: SBMI)
snippet: Silver Bullet Mines Corp. (TSXV: SBMI) published its first assay results on October 8, 2026 from the Columbia and Gold Queen mines in Gila County, Arizona — a two-mine complex acquired in February 2026 and located less than 30 miles from the company's existing mill in Globe, Arizona. The headline result is 41.1 grams per tonne (1.2 oz/t) gold, with samples collected across the Columbia zone, the Gold Queen mine, a previously undocumented Steamboat Mine, and at least four newly identified high-grade gold zones within the complex. Results are guiding the company toward producing higher-grade saleable concentrate at its Globe mill. The company cautions that no NI 43-101 compliant historical technical data has been located for these mines, meaning the 41.1 g/t result should be treated as a surface or selective sample from known mineralized ground rather than a resource-grade proxy. For retail investors evaluating high-grade gold explorers on TSXV, the combination of 41+ g/t surface assays, a nearby permitted mill, and an Arizona Tier 1 jurisdiction addresses three of the five key de-risking factors for early-stage gold projects. Formal resource delineation drilling would be the logical next step.

headline: ALLIED GOLD KURMUK FEEDS FIRST ORE TO CRUSHER — FIRST GOLD POUR IN ETHIOPIA NOW 'IMMINENT'
snippet: Allied Gold Corp. (TSX: AAUC) reported on October 6-7, 2026 that its Kurmuk Mine in the Benishangul-Gumuz region of Ethiopia has successfully energized its national power grid connection and fed first ore through the crushing circuit, with full handover from commissioning to operations in progress. A 1-million tonne ore stockpile has been accumulated, with plans to grow it to 1.5 million tonnes before ramping the grinding circuit. The company described first ore to grinding and first gold as 'imminent.' Allied simultaneously released exploration data showing resource growth potential and mine life extension targets from its 2026 drill program around the Kurmuk deposit. Following commissioning and ramp-up, Kurmuk is expected to produce 240,000-270,000 ounces annually in 2027, making it one of the most significant new East African gold mine startups of the year. Investors should monitor the actual first gold pour announcement, which would represent the transition from developer to producer for Allied Gold — the kind of re-rating catalyst that historically lifts market multiples by 10-30% in gold miners when commissioning completes successfully.

headline: HOT CHILI DRILLS 725M OF CU-AU AT LA VERDE CHILE — WIDEST INTERCEPT YET AS PORPHYRY SCALE FIRMS UP
source_name: Junior Mining Network / Hot Chili Ltd. (ASX: HCH, TSXV: HCH)
snippet: Hot Chili Ltd. (ASX: HCH, TSXV: HCH) published a drilling update on La Verde in Chile's Domeyko Mining District reporting that drillhole DKD039 returned 725 metres grading 0.42% copper equivalent from 18 metres depth — the widest significant intercept in the deposit's drilling history. Twenty-five additional drillhole assays remain pending, meaning the full size of the current drilling round is not yet known. Hot Chili has confirmed a maiden resource estimate and revised prefeasibility study integration with the company's larger Costa Fuego project complex, with the environmental impact assessment submission targeted for Q2 2027. La Verde's porphyry geometry — wide, shallow, near-surface copper-gold mineralization — matches the bulk-tonnage template of Chile's most profitable large copper mines. With LME copper above $14,500 per tonne and copper tariff escalation creating a North American supply imperative, bulk-tonnage Chilean porphyry assets are attracting increasing institutional attention. Hot Chili's Costa Fuego complex (of which La Verde is a component) already hosts a 9.5 million ounce gold equivalent resource; the current drilling is stress-testing whether La Verde's scale can materially move that figure upward ahead of the Q2 2027 EIA submission.
